classification.difficultyReason: Use the scaffolded RHS and SAS congruence arguments and corresponding parts to prove angle and perpendicular bisectors.

content.prompt: Let PS and PT be the two tangents to a circle with centre O from a point P outside the circle.

spec.description: Two tangents PS/PT extended beyond contacts. PO and chord ST meet at M; centre O below M. Original figure has no OS/OT radii or right-angle/equality marks.
spec.answerVisibility: Original supplied givens and targets only; no derived numerical values or proof conclusions.

sizing.exceptionReason: Tall two-tangent proof figure retains distinct P,M,O positions and source chord; inspect final height and10pt label clearance rather than compressing.

answer.short: Congruent by RHS: right angles at S/T, equal radii OS/OT and common hypotenuse OP.
answer.worked: $\angle PSO=\angle PTO=90^\circ$ (radius and tangent), $OS=OT$ (radii), and OP is common. Therefore $\triangle PSO\equiv\triangle PTO$ by RHS.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Hence, prove that the tangents have equal length, and that OP bisects the angle between the tangents and bisects the angle between the radii OS and OT.

answer.short: $PS=PT$, $\angle SPO=\angle TPO$, and $\angle SOP=\angle TOP$ (matching parts).
answer.worked: Matching parts of the congruent triangles give $PS=PT$, $\angle SPO=\angle TPO$, and $\angle SOP=\angle TOP$. Hence OP bisects both the angle between the tangents and the angle between OS and OT.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Join the chord ST and let it meet PO at M.

answer.short: Congruent by SAS: PS=PT, equal angles at P, and PM common.
answer.worked: From part a, $PS=PT$ and $\angle SPM=\angle TPM$. Also PM is common, so $\triangle SPM\equiv\triangle TPM$ by SAS.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Hence, prove that OP is the perpendicular bisector of ST.

answer.short: $SM=TM$ and $OP\perp ST$, by matching parts and the straight angle at M.
answer.worked: Matching parts give $SM=TM$ and $\angle SMP=\angle TMP$. These two adjacent angles lie on straight line ST, so each is $90^\circ$. Thus OP is perpendicular to ST at its midpoint M.
